imageDescript: Tunnel under East Washington -- connecting N Fair Oaks and Wright Street
personText: This should be a positive -- as a safe way to cross East Washington Ave, BUT the tunnel attracts unhomed people -- who sleep in the tunnel. The tunnel is quite often ''littered'' with paper and food scraps, excrement, drug paraphernalia - used syringes, etc. All the aforementioned are a huge danger to my dogs - so I don't use it often.

personText: The path provides a break from the city noise and traffic - and homes with barking dogs in their home/yard - I enjoy the smooth surface that's easy to navigate. (worrying about cracks and potholes on city streets - crossing streets).
dogText: My dog enjoys sniffing and hunting for creatures that have used or crossed the path. (Rodents, deer, squirrels and rabbits). I am typically more relaxed, too. Which provides the dog with a calm companion.
walkText: The path is shared with bicycling commuters and joggers/walkers. So following the path etiquette is important and being aware when others are approaching - can be worrisome -- but expected.

personText: I enjoy this path - away from traffic and city distractions. This path is less secluded which makes walking the path safer. I like the even surface, well marked signage, areas to explore, within minutes from my home.
dogText: My dog loves any walk. This path is well used but always plenty of room to pass and to explore. If I'm happy -- my pup is happy.
walkText: Not secluded is a big plus. I enjoy the paved path for stability and for the views of the State Capitol and the neighborhood without being next to the houses/homes.

personText: Its a lovely little garden bed and I can't wait to look at it and find something new that has popped up.
dogText: my dog loves to look in the thick of it and sniff for creatures, or maybe try to ''leave a message'' -- which isn't allowed by the owner/walker
walkText: its happy little distraction from the hard surfaces and traffic chatter
